title: Tunable Chaos in the Finite Mean SYK Model
authors: Arkaprava Mukherjee, Sumilan Banerjee, Sandip P. Trivedi, Nandini Trivedi
abstract: The complex Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model, featuring fermions with all-to-all interactions, serves as a dual paradigm for understanding non-Fermi liquid behavior and the holographic nature of charged black holes. Two defining characteristics of the standard SYK model are its maximal chaos (Lyapunov exponent $λ_{\mathrm{L}}=2πT$ at temperature $T$), and its finite zero-temperature residual entropy. While previous studies have largely focused on couplings drawn from a zero-mean Gaussian distribution, we investigate a generalized model with a finite mean-to-standard-deviation ratio, $g\equiv J_{0}/δJ$ of the coupling distribution in order to get deeper insight into the evolution of chaos. We find that increasing $g$ yields the following effects: (i) The system remains a fast scrambler with $λ_{\mathrm{L}}=A~T$, but with a suppressed coefficient $A<2π$. (ii) In the limit $g\to \infty$, out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) no longer exhibit exponential growth with $λ_{\mathrm{L}}\simeq 0$. (iii) The spectral correlations indicative of late-time chaos maintain Wigner-Dyson level spacing statistics for all values of $g$. (iv) The system preserves a finite residual entropy, albeit with reduced magnitude, for all $g$ values. We conclude that in this generalized SYK model, there is a chaotic to non-chaotic crossover. Moreover different measures of chaos decouple, demonstrating that the presence of finite residual entropy does not strictly imply maximal chaos.
summary: The paper explores the generalized SYK model by varying the mean-to-standard deviation ratio of its random couplings. It demonstrates a continuous crossover from highly chaotic behavior (maximal scrambling) towards less chaotic regimes as disorder is tuned. This work highlights that different measures of quantum chaos can decouple, providing deeper insights into the relationship between entropy and maximal chaos in strongly correlated systems.
main_problem: The study investigates how tuning the mean-to-standard-deviation ratio ($g$) of random couplings affects the chaotic properties of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model, exploring a crossover between chaotic and non-chaotic regimes.
main_result: Increasing $g$ causes a continuous chaotic-to-non-chaotic crossover in scrambling dynamics; crucially, different measures of chaos decouple, showing that finite residual entropy does not mandate maximal chaos.
method: The analysis employs multiple quantum chaos diagnostics—including Lyapunov exponents (from OTOCs), spectral form factors (SFF), and nearest-neighbor level spacing statistics—across varying disorder parameters.
model_or_system: The system is the generalized Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model, featuring fermions with all-to-all interactions whose complex couplings are drawn from a Gaussian distribution parameterized by $g = J_0/\deltaJ$.
key_observables: Lyapunov exponent ($\lambda_L$), Residual Entropy ($S_0/N$), Out-of-Time Correlators (OTOCs), Spectral Form Factor (SFF), and nearest-neighbor energy level spacing statistics.
important_parameters: The tuning parameter $g = J_0/\deltaJ$, which controls the degree of randomness in the couplings, ranging from $g=0$ (standard SYK) to $g 	o \infty$ (clean limit).
main_assumptions: Numerical simulations rely on Exact Diagonalization (ED) for finite system sizes ($N$), and the analysis assumes self-averaging properties hold in the thermodynamic limit.
figures_summary: Figures summarize the evolution of chaos diagnostics across varying $g$, showing $\lambda_L$ decreasing from $2\pi T$ to zero, while level repulsion persists and residual entropy remains finite.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes spectral density ($ho(E)$), entanglement entropy ($S_A$), and various time-domain chaos measures (OTOCs, SFF) as functions of the disorder parameter $g$, demonstrating the decoupling between these different indicators of quantum chaos.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding how tuning disorder in strongly interacting fermionic systems modifies fundamental concepts like maximal chaos and scrambling, which are central to holographic theories and condensed matter physics.
